Indexed objects

Source: R/tensor-indexed.R
Indexed.Rd

Idx(name, range) is an integer index symbol, as SymPy's Idx; range is an upper bound n (giving 0 to n - 1) or a pair of bounds. IndexedBase(name, shape) returns a function building indexed objects A(i, j) (SymPy's A[i, j]), and Indexed(base, ...) builds one directly. get_indices(e) returns the free indices of an expression and its symmetries; repeated indices in a product are summed (Einstein convention), and the terms of a sum must have the same free indices. get_contraction_structure(e) lists the summations: index tuples with the terms summed over them, NULL for terms without summation, and nested structures for subexpressions, as SymPy's dictionary.

Usage

Idx(name, range = NULL)

IndexedBase(name, shape = NULL)

Indexed(base, ...)

get_indices(e)

get_contraction_structure(e)

format_contraction_structure(cs)

Arguments

name

The name, or a symbol to take it from (an integer symbol for Idx()).

range

An upper bound or a pair of bounds.

shape

Optional dimensions.

base

An IndexedBase function or a name.

...

Indices.

e

An expression.

cs

A contraction structure.

Value

Idx() and Indexed() return expressions; IndexedBase() a function; get_indices() a list of the free indices and the symmetries; get_contraction_structure() a list of key, value pairs.

Examples

i <- Idx("i"); j <- Idx("j")
A <- IndexedBase("A"); x <- IndexedBase("x"); y <- IndexedBase("y")
A(i, j)
#> A[i, j]
get_indices(A(i, j) * x(j))$indices
#> [[1]]
#> i
#> 
format_contraction_structure(get_contraction_structure(x(i)*y(i) + A(j, j)))
#> [1] "{(i,): {x[i]*y[i]}, (j,): {A[j, j]}}"
